correctness.rationale: In characteristic >=5, the partial derivative test gives exactly r=±2 as singular. The point at infinity has contact order four and Hessian weight two. In the affine chart, a direct tangent-line expansion at x≠0 gives the condition f'(y)^2−3f(y)(6y^2+r)=−Phi_r(y)=0 for a flex; the symbolic Hessian restriction also equals 54xPhi_r(y). Independent symbolic calculations confirm the discriminant and resultant in all allowed characteristics. The exclusions make the six y roots distinct and nonzero and keep f(y) nonzero on them; each yields three distinct x roots. At x=0 the four points are simple flexes, with x a local parameter by separability of f; at x≠0 the parameter y and the squarefree Phi show simple Hessian zeros. Over a y residue field the possible cycle structures of x^3=−f(y) are exactly (1,2), (1,1,1), (3) under the stated tests, and base-field orbit lengths multiply by the y orbit degree. The independent replay counted points directly over extensions of degrees 1,2,3, and certified full splitting by degree six, confirming all four F7 rows. The r=3 and r=4 counts are (7,17,13) and (7,17,7) respectively, so the geometric twist is not an F7 isomorphism.
residual_risks: The result describes cycle type, not a preferred labeling of Frobenius. It makes no classification of excluded fibres or the curve zeta function.
